transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Helix - Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Helix - Platform), Dev Patel (Helix - CISO)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side - I'm Alex, I run the AE for this region, and Priya is our SE who will lead the bench and tech details.
00:14 Marta: Hi all, Marta here. thanks. we're trying to scope a POC to decide between hosted, dedicated, or private. main drivers are latency, cost, and data residency.
00:28 Priya: Great. can you walk us through current traffic profiles? qps, typical and worst-case token lengths?
00:37 Marta: Sure. baseline - about 150 rps during peak across customer-facing chat; typical prompt+response ~ 120 tokens total, tail up to 800 tokens in long form. concurrency for we expect around 250 concurrent users, but per-second concurrent requests is maybe 60-80 qps.
00:56 Liam: Also from infra perspective we prefer VPC or private networking for anything PII. production would need SSO and audit logs.
01:06 Alex: Helpful. ok success criteria - what would you consider a win for the POC?
01:11 Marta: Latency p95 under 600ms for typical 128-token interactions, accuracy parity with our baseline model, and cost under X (we said ballpark of $Y per 1M tokens). Also must pass security review for dedicated or private if we go that route.
01:29 Priya: Quick clarifying - when you say accuracy parity, is that relative to your current hosted model? and do you have eval prompts?
01:36 Marta: Yes parity to our current internal model. we'll share eval set - 500 prompts representing customer flows.
01:43 Priya: Perfect, that'll let us run quality regressions. on infra - hosted is fastest to stand up; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput; Private is for strict compliance/data residency. The tradeoffs are cost predictability vs operational isolation.
01:58 Alex: And for Dedicated, we can provision A100 or H100 based pools depending on perf. typical bench we run will show token/s throughput, p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
02:12 Dev: On security... CISO hat - we need SOC 2, encryption at rest with KMS, key ownership, SSO/SAML, and audit logs. private on-prem is preferred if we can't get key ownership and logs to our standards.
02:28 Alex: Understood. Redwood supports KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has managed encryption but we can do customer-managed keys for enterprise tiers. we'll include compliance matrix.
02:40 Priya: For the benchmark plan I'm thinking: 1) run synthetic traffic with your token distribution 2) run eval set for quality/regression 3) run A/B compare hosted vs dedicated under same model version and same concurrency. we'll measure p50/p95, errors, and cost per token.
02:58 Marta: Timeline? we have a product release in mid-June so need POC results by first week of May ideally.
03:06 Alex: that is tight but doable. we'll aim to run initial benchmarks by end of April if you provide sample workload by 04/28.
03:14 Liam: On workload sizing - our peak memory footprint per session is small, but we use a lot of KV cache because we do multi-turn. how does that affect Dedicated sizing?
03:25 Priya: KV cache increases memory but the runtime supports KV cache sharing across requests; Dedicated sizing will be based on model size, expected KV cache retention, and concurrency. we'll propose a Dedicated pool spec, e.g., 8x H100-equivalent for your peak.
03:40 Marta: Cost concerns - what's the delta between hosted and dedicated?
03:44 Alex: Hosted is usage-based and simpler but can be more expensive at scale; Dedicated has a monthly reserved component but lower marginal token cost. we'll send example cost models with your projected volume.
03:56 Marta: Also, we have internal rule that any external cloud provider storing user data in EU must have data residency - can Redwood ensure region pinning?
04:05 Priya: Yes, region pinning is supported for both Hosted and Dedicated; Private on-prem obviously keeps everything in your network. note: Dedicated gives you isolation at the capacity level but control plane metadata may still be hosted unless you take Private.
04:22 Dev: For SOC2 evidence, we need access to audit logs for all requests for 90 days, and ability to snapshot logs for export. can you confirm?
04:32 Alex: We'll include our audit log retention options in the SLA. Dedicated and Private offer extended retention.
04:40 Marta: Back to benchmarks - what GPU types will you run? we want to compare A100 vs H100 and quantized 4-bit options.
04:49 Priya: We'll run both A100 and H100 if available; quantization profiles we'll test 8-bit and 4-bit where model supports it. note that 4-bit can change quality slightly so we'll pair it with the eval set.
05:02 Liam: How about networking - VPC peering or private link options?
05:07 Alex: We support VPC peering and private interconnects for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be used with private endpoints for enterprise.
05:13 Marta: ok great. any concerns about warm starts and cold starts? our sessions are multi-turn and we rely on KV caching to avoid re-encoding.
05:22 Priya: Redwood's runtime keeps KV cache across concurrent sessions and we have strategies for prefix caching. cold start impact is mostly at the first token for a new model shard - we can measure that in bench.
05:35 Marta: got it. can you also measure tokenization differences? we saw small tokenization mismatch between our current infra and open models that affects cost.
05:43 Priya: yes we'll include tokenization comparison as part of bench.
05:48 Alex: next steps recap - we'll share pricing, SLA, and benchmark plan. Helix will share sample prompts and the eval set. Priya will propose test harness.
06:00 Marta: Sounds good. quick question - if Dedicated goes live and we need to scale burst capacity, how is that handled?
06:08 Alex: We offer burst options and autoscaling policies; Dedicated pools can have reserved baseline with burst to shared capacity. we'll show config examples.
06:18 Dev: Regarding key management, for Dedicated can we bring our own KMS keys and rotate them?
06:23 Priya: Yes, BYOK is supported in Dedicated and Private; Hosted enterprise also supports CMKs in supported clouds. rotation policies are supported.
06:33 Marta: Any also note on model rollouts and fallbacks? we need automatic fallback to a smaller model if primary is overloaded.
06:40 Priya: We support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible variants; that's part of the rollout config. we'll include sample routing policies in the doc.
06:50 Alex: Ok, does anyone object to running hosted vs dedicated first for speed?
06:54 Marta: No objection - we want to prove quality and perf quickly. Private is conditional on security gating.
07:00 Liam: For benchmarks, target qps for initial run - can we aim for 60 qps sustained and spikes to 150?
07:08 Priya: Yes that's a good start. we'll ensure harness can replay that distribution.
07:14 Marta: Great. any other blockers?
07:17 Dev: Just need the compliance artifacts, privacy agreements, and data handling docs.
07:22 Alex: We'll send the security pack and SOC2 docs with the next email.
07:28 Marta: timeline again - sample data by 04/28, bench by end of April, results first week of May.
07:35 Alex: Noted. Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench runs.

[End of transcript]

Notes: transcript has minor transcription errors (names, acronyms) typical of automated capture. references to documents: "pricing deck" (link to be sent), "benchmark spreadsheet" (to be shared), "security pack (SOC2, KMS, SSO)" (link to be shared).
